subject: seahorse
pitch: A lined seahorse holding on to a strand of seagrass with its curled tail. A ridged body in sunny yellow with thin dark lines and a few white freckles, a little crown of spikes on its head, a long tube snout, a delicate fluttering fin on its back, and big, curious eyes.
reasoning:
I should aim for solid quality without overengineering, sticking to the well-documented SDK calls I'm confident about—joint, chain, sweep, part, stick, spike, ring, along, surface, membrane—and designing the structure conservatively around those.

Now I'm sketching the seahorse pose: an upright S-curve body facing forward, with the tail curling toward the belly side at the base where it would wrap around a strand of seagrass, scaling the whole figure to roughly 0.35m tall for visual presence.

Working out the spiral geometry for the tail wrapping the strand...

I'm now planning the body radius profile along the path from head to tail, with bulges at the neck and belly and tapering toward the tip, then figuring out how to construct the snout as a tapered rod shape.

For the jaw, I'm separating it into upper and lower pieces with a joint connecting them, and considering using a chain structure for the spine with bone references, though the exact API for chains and joints isn't fully clear so I'm making reasonable assumptions about how they work.

I'll simplify the hierarchy with a root joint at body center, head as its child, and jaw as head's child, parenting the spine chain to root too—good enough even if not perfectly anatomical. For unassigned parts I'll let them snap to the nearest bone automatically, and I'm planning the crown spikes tilted back at the top of the head plus eye spheres with pupils placed symmetrically on either side.

For the dark body rings, rather than relying on unclear path-orientation fields, I'll compute position, tangent, and radius myself using a CatmullRomCurve3, rotating a torus so its axis aligns with the tangent at each sample point—avoiding guesswork about unknown frame conventions.

I'm also planning small freckle spheres scattered near the surface, positioned using the tangent frame's perpendicular basis vectors to offset them around the body at random angles, with flattened scaling for a subtle look.

For the dorsal fin, I'm thinking of an extruded thin membrane shape on the back of the lower trunk, defining a 2D outline with a fan-like ripple and orienting it in the plane spanning the y-axis and backward z-axis, plus adding thin rod-like fin rays for structure.

For seagrass, I'm sweeping a gently curved path from the seabed upward with slight sway for the main strand, adding a couple more swept blades for variety, and rigging the strand to the nearest skeletal joint as a root.

Checking the floor contact: the tail tip and strand base should rest near y=0 so the seahorse looks held up by the grass, and overall model height is set by whichever is taller between the grass and the seahorse. Now I'm plotting the spine path coordinates from head to tail, starting with the head tilted forward and down into the neck curve.

Then I'm computing the tail's spiral coils, working out angle steps, radius, and vertical drop per turn so the coil pitch stays wider than the tail's diameter and ends with a tapered tip near the front.

I realize the wrap radius around the strand axis is too tight relative to the strand and tail thickness, so I widen it slightly and recheck the resulting coordinates. I also catch that a straight vertical strand would pass right through the body's belly, so I need to curve the strand's path as it rises past that region.

Trying to route the strand so it leans backward to clear the body creates a new collision with the dorsal fin's position, so I consider instead offsetting the strand sideways to avoid both the belly and the fin.

I'm working out the radius tapering along the strand's path using arc-length parameterization for smooth thickness changes, and plan to reuse CatmullRomCurve3's arc-length sampling for consistency across rings and freckles too.

Now I'm defining the body's radius profile from neck to tail tip as a piecewise lerp table, and sketching the head geometry—an ellipsoid centered above the spine with a small cylindrical snout extending forward.

I'm continuing the snout taper and adding a thinner lower jaw with a pivot joint, then eyes with white spheres, dark irises, and highlights, plus a brow ridge. For the head crown, I'm placing five spikes along the top in a row with slight backward tilt, darker orange, and then extending spikes down the spine ridge offset along the back normal direction computed from the curve's tangent.

Working out the perpendicular back-normal and side vectors for placing rings, freckles, and spikes consistently along the trunk's curve, then setting up a sparse series of low-poly tori as decorative rings along the trunk up to about 42% of its length, though I'm unsure the segment counts will render cleanly.

For coloring, I'm choosing a yellow body with a lighter cream belly, dark brown accent lines, orange highlights, and white details, and planning small flattened cream plates along the front of the trunk for texture. I'm also sketching tiny pectoral fins near the head using scaled-down spheres, and starting to outline a scalloped dorsal fin shape positioned along the back of the curve using a 2D extrude profile.

Now I'm adding thin dark rods radiating through the dorsal fin using small cylinders, positioning the fin base along the back surface, and planning extra seagrass blades with varied lean and two shades of green plus a sandy floor disc. I'm also setting up the skeleton with a hips root joint and starting the head joint placement.

I'm working through the joint hierarchy carefully, since I'm unsure whether chain() and joint() correctly accept a parent reference without errors, and whether spike() supports a color parameter -- I'll fall back to constructing simple cone geometries manually if the spike signature is unclear.
